title: bug: doctor and moe-proxy project-path checks disagree with the daemon lifecycle's own-path rule
description: doctor.ts:176 path.resolve()s the projectPath that /health reports and compares the two case-sensitively. A daemon spawned with d:\x (VS Code lowercases the drive) therefore false-fails `doctor --project D:\x` with 'port reused by another daemon', and /mnt/<d> versus drive spellings fail the same way. moe-proxy (utils.ts readDaemonInfoResult, daemonIdentity.ts classify) compares its own MOE_PROJECT_PATH unresolved, so a native alias (//x on Linux, /x on Windows) refuses its own daemon. That refusal is a non-destructive exit, and launchers and the cwd always pass canonical paths. The fix is to compare isSameProjectPath(recorded or reported value as written, path.resolve(own)), the rule task-25ba449a applies in index.ts.

implementationPlan.description:
MOE-PROXY OWN-PATH RULE: tests first (RED), then the fix (GREEN). Load test-driven-development.

Prerequisites. dependsOn gates the claim: 724e31fa and 3def0804 (proxy utils.ts lane), 48f0b3aa (WT-16, doctor.ts) and 4ca62c89 (index.ts lane tail).
- Confirm each landed: `git log moe/work-2026-10-24 --grep 'Moe-Task: <id>'`.
- Confirm packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts getProjectPath still returns `process.env.MOE_PROJECT_PATH || process.cwd()` unresolved.
- Confirm it is still the only source of the proxy's own path: index.ts main → connect → readDaemonInfoResult and probeDaemonIdentity.
- If a landed row changed either, stop and call moe.request_replan.

Design: fix it at the single source.
- getProjectPath resolves natively. That is the daemon lifecycle's own-path rule (canonicalProjectPath).
- readDaemonInfoResult, classify and comparableProjectPath stay unchanged: they compare both arguments by the contract, and the recorded or served value stays compared as written.
- Do NOT resolve inside readDaemonInfoResult or classify. Their existing rows pass non-native own paths on purpose: own '\\\\srv\\share\\proj' and '\\\\wsl.localhost\\...' on Linux, and own '/mnt/d/proj' on native Windows. A native resolve there would break those rows.

RED, in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.test.ts describe('getProjectPath'):
- Change 'returns MOE_PROJECT_PATH if set' to expect path.resolve('/custom/path'). That is identical on POSIX and C:\\custom\\path on native Windows.
- Add 'resolves a native alias of its own project, so discovery finds its daemon':
  - mkdtemp a dir, then chdir to path.dirname(dir). Restore the cwd and rm the dir in finally.
  - alias = win32 ? dir.slice(2).replace(/\\/g, '/') : `/${dir}`.
  - Precondition: expect([path.relative(dir, path.resolve(alias)), comparableProjectPath(alias) === comparableProjectPath(dir)]).toEqual(['', false]).
  - Write .moe/daemon.json with projectPath: dir, and set MOE_PROJECT_PATH = alias.
  - expect([getProjectPath(), readDaemonInfoResult(getProjectPath())]).toEqual([dir, { info, retryable: false }]).

RED, in packages/moe-proxy/src/daemonIdentity.test.ts describe('moe-proxy bridges only to a daemon serving its own project'):
- startProxy gains an optional `spell = (dir: string) => dir`, used for MOE_PROJECT_PATH.
- startProxy spawns with cwd: path.dirname(testDir). The drive-less Windows alias needs it; it is harmless for E1–E4.
- Add E5 'opens /mcp when MOE_PROJECT_PATH is a native alias of its project (//x on POSIX, /x on Windows)', in E2's shape:
  - a fake daemon serving testDir, and startProxy(port, HOST, alias);
  - waitFor the upgrade; expect upgrades ['/mcp'] and healthRequests ['GET /health'];
  - end stdin; the proxy exits 0.

On HEAD, the alias row and E5 must fail by assertion: getProjectPath returns the alias, and the proxy exits 1 with 'daemon.json belongs to a different project'. Record that RED in the step note.

GREEN, in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:
- getProjectPath becomes `return path.resolve(process.env.MOE_PROJECT_PATH || process.cwd());`.
- Add a two-line why comment: our own path names a directory on this host; the daemon applies the same rule (canonicalProjectPath); recorded and served paths stay compared as written.
- No other proxy change. Error handling is unchanged: a genuinely foreign daemon.json still exits 1 as non-retryable, and a foreign /health still exits 1.

implementationPlan.description:
DOCTOR USES THE LIFECYCLE'S RULE: tests first (RED), then the fix (GREEN).

RED, in packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.test.ts describe('runDoctor — daemon health reachability'). Reuse startHealthServer, writeDaemonJson and line.
- D1 'passes when /health reports this project in a spelling only the shared path contract equates':
  - reported = win32 ? testDir with its drive letter's case flipped (VS Code lowercases the drive) : `//wsl$/Ubuntu${testDir}`;
  - reach contains '[OK]' and exitCode is 0.
- D2, it.skipIf(win32), 'still fails when /health reports the POSIX path in another case':
  - reported = testDir.toUpperCase();
  - reach contains '[FAIL]' and exitCode is 1.
- D3 'passes for a native alias of --project':
  - chdir to path.dirname(testDir), restored in finally;
  - alias = win32 ? testDir.slice(2) : `/${testDir}`;
  - /health reports testDir; runDoctor(alias) gives '[OK]' and exitCode 0.

On HEAD, D1 fails on both OSes: path.resolve folds neither the drive case nor the WSL share. D2 and D3 pass on HEAD; they are guards. D2 kills over-folding, and D3 kills a fix that stops resolving our own path. The existing 'different project' and 'different pid' rows must stay FAIL.

  - Export canonicalProjectPath, comparableProjectPath and isSameProjectPath.

- packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:
  - Delete the moved definitions and import the three names from './util/projectPath.js'.
  - The export list keeps canonicalProjectPath, comparableProjectPath and isSameProjectPath, now as a re-export. index.test.ts, healthHost.test.ts and the contract table test keep importing them from index.
  - No other index.ts change.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts probeDaemonReachability:
  - projectMatches = typeof body.projectPath === 'string' && isSameProjectPath(body.projectPath, canonicalProjectPath(expectedProjectPath)), imported from '../util/projectPath.js'.
  - Add a one-line comment: this is validateDaemonInfoForProject's rule in index.ts; only our own --project is resolved, and the reported path is compared as written.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe-proxy and `moe-daemon doctor` judge project identity by the daemon lifecycle's own-path rule: isSameProjectPath(the recorded or reported value as written, path.resolve(our own path)). A proxy whose MOE_PROJECT_PATH is a native alias of its project (//x on POSIX, /x on the current Windows drive) finds and bridges to its own daemon. doctor passes a healthy daemon whose /health reports this project under a spelling the shared contract equates: drive-letter case, /mnt/<d> versus drive, or a WSL share. A genuinely different project is still refused or failed.
acceptanceCriteria: A proxy with MOE_PROJECT_PATH set to a native alias reads its daemon.json and opens /mcp: E5, plus the getProjectPath alias row.
doctor reports [OK] when /health names this project as a drive-case flip (Windows) or as //wsl$/<distro><path> (POSIX): D1.
doctor reports [FAIL] when /health names the POSIX path in another case (D2), and still for a different project or pid.
doctor reports [OK] for runDoctor(<native alias of the project>): D3.
dist/index.js still exports comparableProjectPath, with every key in scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs unchanged.
